title: evals: contained A/B harness for skill versions
description:
Build a small, contained runner that executes a task against one or more *arms* — an arm being a specific version of a skill, or no skill at all — in an isolated clean room, then captures the outputs for a human to read.

## Why

Skill changes currently ship on inspection. We have already shipped a change of exactly this shape that failed silently: the "Visual-first sections" authoring rule in `pd-components/dist/llms.txt`. `docs/pd-visual-redesign-research.md` records the outcome — "most agent-generated docs use `<md>` prose everywhere" — and we only found out informally, long after. That is the case for measuring rather than assuming.

## Design

**An arm is a parameter.** This makes "with vs without a skill" and "version A vs version B" the same mechanism — `--arm none` is just another arm. A list of one arm is a single-arm exploration run rather than an A/B: useful for trying a new skill idea in isolation, away from this repo's ~30 skills, CLAUDE.md and hooks, which otherwise contaminate any local test. Adding `--arm none` graduates an exploration into an experiment with one flag.

**Judgement is a human reading the outputs.** No graders, no LLM judges, no rubrics. Those are downstream of knowing what "good" looks like, which for the motivating case we do not yet know. The one automated check is whether the skill was actually invoked (see the invocation phase) — that guards a silent, self-deceiving failure where both arms are effectively the same run.

**Do not redesign the cell.** `src/assurance/evals/run.sh:157-222` (`run_agent_arm_live`) is already ~80% of it: mktemp workspace outside the repo (claude walks up and finds `.git`), credential copy, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocation, skill installed into `$CFG/skills/<name>`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `bypassPermissions`, `< /dev/null`, stream-json capture, workspace copied out. Lift it. The isolation recipe is verified in `docs/headless-claude-cli-evals.md`.

## Shape

Python + uv module at `src/evals/`, driven by `make evals` and `uv run python -m evals`. Named plural deliberately: `eval` is a shell builtin, so a bare `eval` on PATH would be shadowed and `evals run --skill x` would execute `run --skill x` as a shell command.

```
evals run --skill <name> --arm <ref|WORKTREE|none> [--arm ...] \
         --scenario <dir> [--n 1] [--invoke instructed|organic] [--model ...]
 evals list | show <run-id> | clean
```

## Out of scope

Graders, LLM judges, rubrics. Multi-host (Claude only; if Codex/Grok are added later, `stream.jsonl` parsing breaks and the Compound Engineering trailer protocol is the migration path — see `docs/compound-engineering-evals.md`). PATH shims, read-only enforcement, statistical aggregation, CI integration (this bills real tokens).

Refactoring `src/assurance/evals/run.sh` to call this tool is deliberately deferred — breaking a working eval to build a speculative one is a bad trade. Tracked separately.

## Verification strategy

Every phase carries its own gate; skills-7k7.7 confirms what is already proven piecewise rather than being the first moment anything is checked.

- **skills-7k7.8 runs first and blocks everything.** The clean-room recipe is stamped "verified against Claude Code 2.1.175" and we run 2.1.260. Isolation failing is silent and voids every result downstream, so it is re-verified before a line is built on it — with a negative control, because two green results from an insensitive probe is exactly the failure being guarded against.
- **skills-7k7.9 (stub runner) gates the phases that need fast tests.** Without an offline lane every check costs a billed multi-minute run, and the plumbing never gets regression-tested.
- **Isolation canaries run on every cell**, not once: config dir outside the repo, no repo ancestor above the workspace, installed skill set exactly as placed. All filesystem checks, zero cost.
- **The invocation detector gets a negative control** (skills-7k7.4). An untested detector is worse than none, because it will be trusted.
- **`pytest` at `src/evals/tests/`**, matching `src/assurance/tests/` and the existing `make test`.

## Success Criteria

A single command runs one task against two arms in isolation and produces a run directory a human can read side by side, with the skill's actual invocation and file reads recorded. Validated on a real-repo scenario where the with/without difference is unmissable (skills-7k7.7) before being trusted on anything subtle.
acceptance_criteria: A single command runs one task against two arms in isolation and produces a run directory a human can read side by side, with the skill's actual invocation and file reads recorded. Validated on a real-repo scenario where the with/without difference is unmissable (skills-7k7.7) before being trusted on anything subtle.

title: evals: walking skeleton — single arm, end to end
description:
Walking skeleton: thread every layer end to end with one arm, one trial, an inline prompt. Later phases thicken this; nothing else starts until a run completes and produces a readable artifact.

## Do

1. `src/evals/` as a uv module (`pyproject.toml`, `__main__.py`), plus a `make evals` target.
2. `evals run --skill <name> --arm WORKTREE --prompt "..."` only.
3. Resolve WORKTREE: run `src/compile.py`, then copy `skills/<name>/` — `skills/` is compiled output, so a stale tree would silently evaluate the last-compiled version. Fail loudly if compile fails.
4. Build the cell, lifted from `src/assurance/evals/run.sh:157-222`: `mktemp -d` base outside the repo (keep the "claude walks up and finds .git" comment — it is the reason), `config/` + `ws/`, copy `~/.claude/.credentials.json` into config, install the skill at `$CFG/skills/<name>/`.
5. Invoke: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$CFG claude -p "$prompt" --output-format stream-json --verbose --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode bypassPermissions --model "$MODEL" < /dev/null`. Capture `stream.jsonl` and `err.txt`; extract the final result envelope to `out.md`.
6. Write to `runs/<run-id>/<arm>/<trial>/` — `skill/` (exactly what was installed), `ws/`, `stream.jsonl`, `out.md`, `err.txt`. Runs accumulate; do not clear previous ones (the current assurance harness wipes its inspect dir on every run and keeps only the last, which is the behaviour to avoid).
7. Emit a minimal `REPORT.md` naming the arm and the paths to open.

## Notes

Keeping `skill/` matters: "what exactly was in arm B?" is the first question asked when a result surprises you.

`runs/` must be gitignored.

## Verification

Isolation canaries, asserted on **every** cell, not once (all filesystem checks — no agent, no cost):

- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` resolves to a path outside the repo tree
- the workspace has no repo ancestor — walk up from cwd and assert this repo's root is never reached
- the config dir's skill set is exactly what we installed, and nothing else

**Do not hard-code the built-in skill floor.** skills-7k7.8 found it drifts between CLI versions (14 on 2.1.175, 13 on 2.1.260, with membership changes). Assert on the *config dir contents* — which we control — never on the agent's visible skill list. If a run ever needs the visible list, measure it per run and compare arms against each other, not against a constant.

Plus one live end-to-end run on a trivial prompt: the run directory contains `skill/`, `ws/`, `stream.jsonl`, `out.md`, `err.txt`, and `out.md` is non-empty. This is the walking skeleton's passing check — the phase is not done without it.

## Acceptance Criteria

A single command runs a real prompt in isolation and leaves an inspectable run directory containing the installed skill, the workspace, the transcript and the final output.
acceptance_criteria: Isolation canaries pass on every cell (config dir outside repo, no repo ancestor above workspace, installed skill set exactly as placed). One live run on a trivial prompt leaves a run directory containing skill/, ws/, stream.jsonl, out.md, err.txt with out.md non-empty.

title: evals: close two open isolation questions (walk-up rule, floor discrepancy)
description:
Two isolation questions left open by skills-7k7.8 and skills-7k7.1. Both are cheap, and both could silently void results if wrong.

## 1. Is Claude Code's project-root walk-up name-based or content-based?

`skills-7k7.1` found this machine has an empty `/tmp/.git` directory (dated Jul 9) that git itself does not recognise — `git -C /tmp rev-parse` reports "not a repository". The canary in `src/evals/canaries.py` was correctly hardened to test for a real repo (`.git/HEAD` present, or `.git` as a gitlink file) rather than the `.git` name.

But that hardening cuts both ways. **We do not know whether the CLI's own walk-up uses the same rule.** If Claude Code's project detection is name-based, then `/tmp` counts as a project root for it, and anything dropping a `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/` into `/tmp` would leak context into every clean room — while our canary stayed green, because it deliberately tolerates that empty `.git`.

Neither `/tmp/CLAUDE.md` nor `/tmp/.claude` exists today, so there is no live leak. The guarantee currently rests on that absence, not on any check we control. That is the gap.

**Probe:** drop a marker `CLAUDE.md` in `/tmp` containing a distinctive token, run one clean-room cell, check whether the token reaches the agent, remove the marker. One cheap call.

**If name-based:** the canary must additionally assert no `CLAUDE.md` / `.claude/` exists in any ancestor of the workspace, regardless of git status — and `mktemp -d` under `/tmp` may need reconsidering.

## 2. Reconcile the built-in floor measurement

`docs/headless-claude-cli-evals.md` has been corrected: the init event is ground truth, self-report is not, and the two disagreed by 4-5 entries on the same CLI version. Confirm the corrected section matches what a fresh run actually emits, and check whether the floor differs between a subagent-spawned cell and a top-level one — the two measurements were taken in different contexts, which is one candidate explanation for the discrepancy.

## Verification

Probe 1 is conclusive in one direction or the other: the marker token either reaches the agent or it does not. Do not report "probably fine" — run it. Remove the marker afterwards regardless of outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

The walk-up rule is established empirically and recorded in `docs/headless-claude-cli-evals.md`. If name-based, `src/evals/canaries.py` gains the ancestor `CLAUDE.md`/`.claude` assertion and a test that fails without it. The floor discrepancy has a stated cause or is recorded as unexplained with both measurements preserved.

title: evals: invocation detector false-positives on a failed Skill call
description:
The invocation detector reports a **false positive** for the exact case it was built to guard. Found by the live gate `skills-7k7.7`, which failed check 2.

## The bug

`--invoke instructed` tells the agent to invoke the skill. In the `none` arm the skill does not exist, so the CLI emits a `Skill` tool_use that comes back `<tool_use_error>Unknown skill: rich-doc</tool_use_error>`.

`src/evals/invocation.py:205` decides `invoked` from the `tool_use` block alone and never inspects the matching `tool_result`. Measured on run `20260904-141016-aef7180`:

| field | `none` arm | truth |
|---|---|---|
| `invoked` | `true` | false — skill absent |
| `registered` | `false` | correct |

**Consequence:** the `SKILL NOT INVOKED` banner never fires for a with/without run under `instructed` — the harness's only automated check is inert for its primary use case, while appearing to work. A detector that is trusted and wrong is worse than none, which is the thing this check exists to prevent.

The correct signal is already captured beside it: `registered` (membership in `init.skills`) is right in both arms.

## Why the negative control missed it — the important part

`skills-7k7.4`'s negative control passed, in **stub mode**. The stub models "skill absent" as *no `Skill` call at all* (`runners.py:287`, `if inv.skill_name:`) and never emits a failed tool call at all (`runners.py:214`, `"is_error": False`). Reality is *a `Skill` call that errors*.

**The stub was too kind: it modelled the world the implementer imagined, and the negative control passed against that world rather than against the CLI.** Record this in `src/evals/README.md` under the design findings, and add it to `src/eval-engineer/` anti-patterns — it generalises well past this harness.

## Do

1. Fix detection: treat a `Skill` call whose `tool_result` is an error as **not invoked**. Prefer corroborating with `registered` rather than replacing one single signal with another.
2. **Fix the stub first, or the fix cannot be tested.** The stub must emit a failed `Skill` call (with its error `tool_result`) when `--invoke instructed` runs against an arm with no skill installed.
3. Also fix the read-list undercount: the `Skill` tool loads `SKILL.md` without a `Read` call, so "files read from the skill" reports empty for a genuinely-invoked arm. In run `…-aef7180` the real evidence was a `Bash` line running `config/skills/rich-doc/scripts/pd-lint.mjs`. Either count the `Skill` load itself or stop reporting a read count as invocation evidence.

## Verification

The negative control must now fail against the *old* code — mutation-check it. Re-run the two-arm case in stub mode AND confirm against the committed live transcript at `runs/20260904-141016-aef7180/none/1/stream.jsonl`, which contains a real failed `Skill` call. Commit that transcript as a test fixture; it is the ground truth the stub got wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

`none` under `--invoke instructed` reports NOT INVOKED with the banner, verified against the real recorded transcript and not only against the stub. The stub emits a failed `Skill` call for an absent skill. Reverting the fix fails a test.

title: evals: REPORT.md is not usable for side-by-side reading
description:
`skills-7k7.7` check 4 failed: `REPORT.md` works as an index but not for the side-by-side reading it exists to support.

Judgement in this harness is a human reading two outputs. `REPORT.md` is the entry point to that, so its usability *is* the product, not decoration.

## Observed on run `20260904-141016-aef7180`

- No output preview or excerpt — you cannot see what either arm produced without opening files yourself.
- No file-type or size line. The arms produced `.md` (399 lines, 19 KB) and `.html` (415 lines, 24 KB); the report shows neither.
- The two arms' facts are split across three sections instead of one comparison table, so nothing is actually side by side.
- It lists an "installed skill" path for the `none` arm **that does not exist** — `none` installs nothing by design.

## Do

- One comparison table, arms as columns: invocation status, output file, type, size, and any cheap structural counts already available.
- A short excerpt or head of each arm's primary output, so the difference is visible without leaving the report.
- Do not print paths that do not exist. For `none`, say so explicitly rather than naming a phantom directory.

Keep it plain text and scannable. This is a reading aid, not a grader — no scoring, no verdict, no judgment of which arm is better.

## Verification

Regenerate against the existing run `20260904-141016-aef7180` (already on disk, no billing needed) and read it as a human would. The markdown-vs-pd-components difference must be apparent from the report alone. Assert no non-existent path is printed for a `none` arm.

## Acceptance Criteria

`REPORT.md` for a two-arm run shows both arms side by side with type, size and an excerpt, prints no phantom paths, and makes the observable difference apparent without opening the output files.

title: evals: --scenario with a relative path fails (setup.sh exit 127)
description:
`--scenario <relative-path>` fails. Found during `skills-7k7.7`.

## Repro

```
make evals ARGS='run --skill rich-doc --arm none \
  --scenario src/evals/scenarios/datasette-parquet-renderer --invoke instructed'
```

`setup.sh` exits **127** ("No such file or directory").

## Cause

`scenarios.load` keeps the supplied path relative, and `_run_setup` executes it with `cwd=` the staging dir — so the relative path no longer resolves. An absolute path works, which is the workaround used to complete `skills-7k7.7`.

## Fix

Resolve the scenario path to absolute in `load()`.

## Verification

A test that passes a relative scenario path and asserts the run completes — it must fail against the current code.

## Acceptance Criteria

`--scenario` accepts a relative path, and a regression test fails without the fix.

title: evals: wire report rebuild to the CLI and persist per-cell exit codes
description:
Two small gaps left by `skills-7k7.12`, both about regenerating and reading a report after the fact.

## 1. `rebuild()` is not reachable from the CLI

`report.rebuild(run_dir)` regenerates a report from a run directory with no billing — exactly what you want after changing `report.py`, or when returning to an old run. It is currently a module function only, so using it means writing Python.

Add `evals report <run-id>`. Touches `__main__.py` and possibly `manage.py`, which `skills-7k7.12` deliberately left alone to avoid colliding with concurrent work.

## 2. Per-cell exit codes are not persisted

The run tree never records the agent's exit code, so `rebuild()` infers it from each transcript's `result.is_error` and stamps a `- note:` line admitting the inference. `write_report` already accepts `int | None`, so the plumbing is there — the value just is not written at run time.

Persist the real exit code per cell (alongside `invocation.json` or in the per-arm manifest) and have `rebuild()` prefer it, falling back to inference only for older runs that predate the change.

## Verification

`evals report <run-id>` regenerates a byte-identical report to the one written at run time, for a run created after the exit-code change. For an older run it still works, and still carries the inference note.

## Acceptance Criteria

`evals report <run-id>` exists and regenerates without billing; new runs record a real per-cell exit code and their reports carry no inference note; pre-existing runs still regenerate with the note.

title: evals: NOT INVOKED banner cries wolf on every with/without run
description:
The `SKILL NOT INVOKED` banner fires on **every** legitimate with/without run, and two of its sentences are false when it does. Found by `skills-7k7.7`'s second run (which otherwise passed all five checks).

## Observed on run `20260907-122025-a49bc2a`

Ground truth: `none: invoked=false` (correct — it called, the call errored), `WORKTREE: invoked=true`. A textbook healthy with/without comparison. The banner nonetheless says:

> Arms with no `Skill` call for `rich-doc`: `none`
> The prompt explicitly asked for this skill and **the transcript shows no `Skill` call for it**. **This run is not a comparison** — every arm below ran without the skill, so any difference between them is sampling noise.

Both bolded claims are false here:

1. The transcript **does** show a `Skill` call for `none`. It was made and returned `<tool_use_error>Unknown skill: rich-doc</tool_use_error>`. "No call" and "a call that failed" are different facts, and the harness now distinguishes them internally (`failed_skill_calls`) but not in the banner.
2. **The run *is* a comparison.** `WORKTREE` invoked the skill. Saying otherwise inverts the reader's conclusion about a perfectly good result.

`src/evals/report.py:557-570`.

## Why this is P1, not cosmetic

A `none` arm is *supposed* to not invoke the skill — that is what a baseline is. So the banner fires on every correct with/without run, always crying wolf.

**A detector that always fires is exactly as useless as one that never fires — the same failure, opposite sign.** `skills-7k7.11` fixed the never-fires half. This is the other half: readers will learn within a handful of runs that the red banner is noise and stop reading it, at which point a genuine silent failure sails through unnoticed. That is precisely the outcome the invocation check exists to prevent.

## Do

Fire the banner only when the run is *actually* compromised — no arm that was expected to invoke the skill did so. Specifically:

- An arm with **nothing installed** (`none`) not invoking is expected. Never alarm on it; state it as a normal fact in the comparison table.
- Alarm when an arm **with the skill installed** failed to invoke it, or when *every* arm failed to.
- Distinguish "no `Skill` call" from "a `Skill` call that errored" in the wording — the data already separates them.

## Verification

Regenerate against `20260907-122025-a49bc2a` (already on disk, no billing): no banner, and the `none` arm's non-invocation shown as an expected baseline fact. Then assert the banner still fires for a genuinely compromised run — reuse `20260904-141016-aef7180`, or a synthesised case where an installed arm did not invoke. Both directions must be tested; a fix that only silences the false alarm recreates `skills-7k7.11`.

## Acceptance Criteria

A healthy with/without run produces no alarm banner. A run where an installed arm failed to invoke still does. Tests cover both directions and fail if either is inverted.

title: evals: arms — none / WORKTREE / git-ref, as a list
description:
Make the arm a parameter, and accept a list. This is the change that turns a skill-specific harness into a general one.

## Do

1. `--arm` repeatable. Resolve three forms:
   - `none` — install nothing (baseline arm)
   - `WORKTREE` — compile, then copy from disk
   - `<git-ref>` — `git archive <ref> -- skills/<name>`
2. Loop arms; each gets its own fresh cell and its own `runs/<run-id>/<arm>/` subtree. Arms must never share a workspace.
3. Record each arm's resolved SHA (or `WORKTREE` plus working-tree dirty state) for the manifest.

## Why WORKTREE matters

`git archive` cannot see an uncommitted edit. Evaluating a change *before* committing it is the entire author loop — without this you must commit in order to test, which inverts the workflow.

## Notes

A list of one arm is legal and meaningful: that is the single-arm exploration mode, not a degenerate A/B.

## Verification

In stub mode (skills-7k7.9), assert the three arm forms resolve to *different* installed skill contents from one command:

- `none` — no `skills/` directory exists in the config dir at all
- `WORKTREE` — installed content matches the compiled working tree byte for byte
- `<git-ref>` — installed content matches `git archive` at that ref, and differs from WORKTREE when the tree is dirty

Each arm's manifest entry records the resolved SHA. Arms must write to disjoint paths; assert no shared workspace.

## Acceptance Criteria

`evals run --skill rich-doc --arm none --arm WORKTREE --prompt "..."` produces two independent run subtrees from one command.
acceptance_criteria: The three arm forms resolve to demonstrably different installed skill contents from one command, each recording its resolved SHA, writing to disjoint paths. Verified in stub mode.

title: evals: scenario directories + clone cache
description:
Accept a scenario directory so a task can be re-run reproducibly, and so the workspace can be *prepared* (cloning a real repo) rather than only copied.

## Do

1. `--scenario <dir>`, containing:
   - `prompt.md` (required)
   - `setup.sh` (optional) — run inside the workspace before the agent, lifting `src/assurance/evals/run.sh:183-186`
   - `fixture/` (optional) — static files copied in
   Keep `--prompt "..."` as the inline shorthand for throwaways.
2. Clone cache: scenarios whose `setup.sh` fetches a real repo must not re-fetch per arm per trial. Fetch once into a cache dir, copy per cell.
3. `scenarios/` lives in the module. A "catalog" is just `ls scenarios/` — no catalog code.

## Format

Deliberately the same shape as `src/assurance/evals/cases/` (`prompt.md` + `setup.sh` + `fixture/`), minus the grader files (`checks.sh`, `rubric.md`) we are not carrying over. Do not invent a new format.

## Pinning is a rule, not a preference

`setup.sh` must `git checkout <sha>`, never float. Two reasons: a floating clone makes the scenario drift under you; and for a "plan how to add feature X" task, if X was later merged upstream a floating clone hands the agent the answer. That is `eval-engineer`'s contaminated-checkout anti-pattern.

## Verification

- Stub-mode test: a scenario directory parses, `setup.sh` runs inside the workspace, `fixture/` lands where expected.
- Cache reuse: run two trials and assert the second performs no network fetch (drop a marker in the cache dir on fetch and assert it is not rewritten). Timing alone is not proof.
- Pinning: assert `setup.sh` contains a literal 40-character SHA and no bare branch name — a floating fixture should fail the check, not be caught by review.

## Acceptance Criteria

A scenario directory that clones a pinned real repo runs to completion, and a second trial reuses the cached clone instead of re-fetching.
acceptance_criteria: A scenario with a pinned real repo runs to completion; a second trial provably performs no network fetch (marker file unchanged, not just faster); a scenario with a floating ref fails the pin check.

title: evals: invocation + files-read check from stream.jsonl
description:
Detect whether the skill was actually invoked, and which files it read. This is the only automated check in the harness, and it exists to guard the one failure that is silent and self-deceiving.

## The failure it prevents

If the skill never fires, both arms are effectively the same run — and you will sit comparing two outputs, inventing explanations for a difference that is pure sampling noise. Every other failure mode in this design announces itself. This one lies to you.

## Do

1. Parse `stream.jsonl` for `tool_use` blocks. `check_skill_used()` at `src/assurance/evals/run.sh:72-88` already proves the grep pattern for the `Skill` tool.
2. Collect per arm, into `invocation.json`:
   - was the skill invoked (bool)
   - every `Read` path, normalised and filtered to skill-relative paths
   - `Bash` commands run (rich-doc shells out to `pd-lint.mjs`; useful signal)
3. Surface `SKILL NOT INVOKED` loudly at the top of `REPORT.md`.
4. `--invoke instructed|organic`:
   - `instructed` (default) appends "invoke skill X before you begin" to the prompt. Tests the skill's *content*. Right for version A/B.
   - `organic` appends nothing. Tests the *description*'s routing. Here "did it fire" is itself the result, not a precondition.

## Why this beats a self-reported trailer

Compound Engineering's harness requires hosts to emit a `FILES_READ:` trailer because it supports four host CLIs with different output formats (see `docs/compound-engineering-evals.md`). We are Claude-only and have `stream-json`, so we can read the actual tool calls: ground truth rather than a declaration, at zero prompt-token cost. If multi-host is ever added, the trailer protocol is the migration path.

## Note

This answers the question human inspection cannot: did it open the reference? You can see form choices in the output; you cannot see which files were loaded.

## Verification

**Negative control is mandatory.** A detector nobody tested is worse than no detector, because it will be trusted:

- `--arm none --invoke instructed` must report **NOT INVOKED**. If it reports invoked, the check is broken.
- a run where the skill *was* invoked must report invoked, with a non-empty read list

Commit one real `stream.jsonl`, recorded from a live run in skills-7k7.1, as a `pytest` fixture. The parser is then unit-testable with no network and no billing, and stays regression-tested as the stream format shifts.

## Acceptance Criteria

A run where the skill silently failed to load is impossible to mistake for a real comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Negative control passes: --arm none --invoke instructed reports NOT INVOKED. Positive case reports invoked with a non-empty read list. A recorded stream.jsonl fixture unit-tests the parser with no network.

title: evals: run management — list, show, clean, manifest, --n
description:
Make runs manageable and auditable rather than one-shot.

## Do

1. `manifest.json` per run: skill, arms with resolved SHAs, scenario or prompt, model, invoke mode, trial count, timestamps.
2. `evals list` — runs newest first, with skill, arms and date.
3. `evals show <run-id>` — print the inspection paths and the invocation summary. This is the everyday entry point.
4. `evals clean` — drop old runs.
5. `--n <int>` (default 1) — repeat each arm N times into `<arm>/<trial>/`.

## On --n

This exists so you are not fooled by a single sample when eyeballing, not to do statistics. It performs no aggregation and computes no medians. `REPORT.md` must state the trial count so it is always obvious which you are looking at.

## Verification

Stub-mode round trip: create three runs, assert `list` returns them newest-first, `show` prints paths that exist on disk, `clean` removes what it claims and nothing else. Assert `manifest.json` round-trips — reading it back reconstructs skill, arms, resolved SHAs, scenario, model, invoke mode and trial count.

Assert `--n 3` produces three trial subdirectories per arm and that `REPORT.md` states the trial count.

## Acceptance Criteria

Runs accumulate, are listable, and every run records enough provenance to reconstruct what was compared.
acceptance_criteria: Stub-mode round trip: three runs list newest-first, show prints paths that exist, clean removes only what it claims, manifest.json round-trips fully, and --n 3 yields three trial dirs per arm with the count stated in REPORT.md.

title: evals: README + stated limitations
description:
Write the limitations down now, while they are known, rather than discovering them later. `README.md` in the module, plus an entry in the docs index.

## Must state

- **Claude-only.** If Codex/Grok are added later, `stream.jsonl` parsing breaks; the Compound Engineering trailer protocol is the migration path.
- **With/without under `instructed` carries a prompt confound** — you cannot tell an arm to invoke a skill it does not have, so the arms differ in prompt as well as skill. `src/assurance/evals/run.sh:194-196` already acknowledges this. Prefer `organic` for with/without where the skill routes reliably.
- **N=1 by default.** One pair can mislead. The tool will not stop you; `REPORT.md` states the sample size so you never forget which you are reading.
- **Component-library confound for `rich-doc` specifically** — it curls `llms.txt` from a CDN pinned to `{{ pd-version }}`, so two arms can differ by component version as well as SKILL.md. Pin both arms to the same version or the result is uninterpretable.
- **Not a sandbox.** `bypassPermissions` with real credentials in a temp dir. Fixtures must be disposable.
- **Never in CI.** It bills real tokens.

## Also

Run `auto doc fix` so the docs index picks it up. Cross-link from `src/eval-engineer/` — that skill's harness table currently points at `docs/headless-claude-cli-evals.md` and `src/assurance/evals/` for the single-shot row; this tool becomes the reference implementation for it.

## Verification

Each of the six limitations names the specific thing that breaks, not a vague caution. `auto doc fix` runs clean and the docs index picks up the new entry. `eval-engineer`'s harness table points at this tool for the single-shot row.

## Acceptance Criteria

Someone picking this up cold knows what the tool cannot tell them, without running it first.
acceptance_criteria: All six limitations state the specific failure, auto doc fix runs clean, docs index updated, and eval-engineer's harness table points here for the single-shot row.

title: evals: validate the harness — with/without rich-doc on pinned datasette
description:
Final gate: confirm end to end what the earlier phases proved piecewise. Every phase carries its own verification, so this is not the first check — it is the one that exercises all of them together on a case whose result should be unmissable. If the harness cannot show *that* clearly, it cannot be trusted on anything subtle.

## The scenario — `scenarios/datasette-parquet-renderer/`

**Fixture:** `simonw/datasette` at `bdc973174096cae350ddaa733a10ed8b3ffd970b` (v1.0a38).

Fetch the tree as a tarball, not a clone — `https://codeload.github.com/simonw/datasette/tar.gz/<sha>`. Measured: 0.37 s to fetch and extract, 0.01 s to copy per cell, ~6 MB / 329 files. History is what makes a repo slow, and we do not need it; this also pins harder than a clone, since there is no history for the agent to mine.

(If a scenario ever needs real git, use `git init && git fetch --depth 1 origin <sha> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`. Tarball is the default.)

**Task:** write a design doc for adding a **Parquet output renderer** — so table and query results can be downloaded as `.parquet` alongside the existing `.json` and `.csv`.

**Arms:** `none` vs `WORKTREE`, `--skill rich-doc`.

## Why this feature

- **Absent at this SHA.** Verified: no occurrence of "parquet" anywhere in the tree. The answer is not in the checkout.
- **Grounded.** The `register_output_renderer` hook exists in `datasette/hookspecs.py:72`, and `datasette/blob_renderer.py` is an in-tree exemplar, so a good plan has something real to follow rather than inventing an architecture.
- **Crosses layers.** Hook registration, streaming response, content type, an optional-dependency decision (pyarrow), CLI surface, docs, tests.
- **Has a genuine design tension.** Parquet is columnar, so it cannot stream row-by-row the way the CSV renderer does — buffer the whole result set, or chunk into row groups? A good design doc surfaces that trade-off; a weak one misses it. That gives the output something worth diagramming, which is exactly what should differentiate the two arms.

## Expected difference

Without the skill: plain hand-rolled HTML, or markdown. With it: a `pd-components` doc — tabs, a diagram of the render path, a file-change tree, a decision record for the streaming trade-off. Close to binary, which is what a validation case needs.

## What is being validated

The **harness**, not the skill:

- the two arms are genuinely isolated (arm `none` shows no trace of `rich-doc`)
- the invocation check fires correctly in both directions
- the fixture cache works across arms and trials
- `REPORT.md` is actually usable for side-by-side reading
- a real-repo run completes without timing out

## Then, and only then

The motivating case — the `rich-doc` visual-forms change — is a *version* A/B where the signal is far finer-grained. Do not attempt it until this validation reads cleanly, or an ambiguous result is uninterpretable: skill, or harness?

## Note for later

When we move from harness validation to evaluating *planning* skills, `starship/starship` is the better fixture: "add a new prompt module" is a bounded feature with a consistent known-good shape (config schema + module impl + registration + tests + docs). Also watch for training-data contamination on very famous repos — a model can plan from memory rather than from the checkout, which would quietly invalidate a planning eval. It does not matter here, where document *form* is what is under test.

## Acceptance Criteria

The with/without difference is obvious on inspection, and all five harness checks above are confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: The with/without difference is obvious on inspection, and all five harness checks are confirmed: arms genuinely isolated, invocation check fires in both directions, fixture cache works across arms and trials, REPORT.md usable for side-by-side reading, real-repo run completes without timing out.

title: evals: re-verify clean-room isolation on Claude Code 2.1.260
description:
Re-verify the clean-room isolation conditions against the CLI version we actually run, before building anything on top of them.

## Why this is not a formality

`docs/headless-claude-cli-evals.md` carries the recipe the whole harness depends on, and stamps it: *"Verified empirically against Claude Code 2.1.175… re-verify the two conditions below if the CLI version moves a lot."*

We are on **2.1.260**. That is 85 patch versions past the verification, on a doc that names its own expiry. Isolation failing is silent — a leaked `CLAUDE.md` or the repo's ~30 skills bleeding into the `none` arm produces plausible output that is quietly worthless, and every result downstream of it is void.

## The two conditions

1. **cwd must be outside the repo tree.** Claude Code walks *up* from cwd and re-discovers a parent repo's project skills and `CLAUDE.md` regardless of `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Running under `.tmp/` leaks everything back in.
2. **Do NOT pass `--setting-sources ''`.** It isolates, but also suppresses discovery of the skill-under-test — silently breaking the with-skill arm.

## Verification

Three probes, each a single cheap `claude -p` call asking the agent to list every skill it can see and print its cwd:

- **Negative control (must leak):** cwd inside the repo tree. If this does *not* surface this repo's skills or CLAUDE.md, the probe is not sensitive and proves nothing — fix the probe before trusting the positive results.
- **Condition 1 (must be clean):** cwd from `mktemp -d`, relocated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Must report none of this repo's skills and no CLAUDE.md content.
- **Condition 2 (must still discover):** same, plus one skill installed at `$CFG/skills/<name>/`. Must see exactly that one skill and no others.

The negative control is the point. Two green results with an insensitive probe is the exact failure this issue exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria

All three probes run against Claude Code 2.1.260 with the expected outcomes, including the negative control leaking as predicted. `docs/headless-claude-cli-evals.md` updated with the new verified-against version and any behaviour that changed. If a condition no longer holds, that is a finding — record it and stop, rather than working around it silently.

title: evals: stub runner — offline fast lane for plumbing tests
description:
Port the offline runner seam so everything except the agent's judgment is testable in milliseconds, with no network and no billing.

## Why

Without this, every check in this epic needs a live billed agent run taking minutes. Plumbing — arm resolution, directory layout, manifest, stream parsing, report generation, cache reuse — cannot be iterated on or regression-tested. `src/assurance/evals/run.sh` already solves this with `AGENT_RUNNER=stub` (`run.sh:103-155`, dispatched at `run.sh:92-101`); reuse the pattern rather than inventing one.

## Do

1. A runner seam: `live` (spawn `claude -p`) vs `stub` (write a canned `stream.jsonl` + result envelope, populate the workspace from the fixture).
2. The stub must emit a **realistic** `stream.jsonl` — real `tool_use` blocks for `Skill`, `Read` and `Bash` — so the invocation parser (skills-7k7.4) is exercised by it rather than bypassed.
3. Stub arms must produce a byte-identical run-directory *shape* to live arms. If the shapes diverge, tests pass against a layout that never ships.

## Verification

`pytest` at `src/evals/tests/`, matching `src/assurance/tests/test_compiler.py` and the existing `make test` target. A full stub run completes with no network access and produces a run tree that passes the same structural assertions as a live one.

## Acceptance Criteria

`make test` exercises a complete end-to-end run in stub mode in under a second, and the resulting run directory is structurally indistinguishable from a live run.

title: assurance evals: reuse the evals harness instead of own cell copy
description:
Once `evals` (skills-7k7) is proven, refactor `src/assurance/evals/run.sh` to call it instead of carrying its own copy of the cell.

`run_agent_arm_live()` at `run.sh:157-222` is the code `evals` was extracted from. Two copies will drift.

Deliberately deferred out of the epic: breaking a working eval to build a speculative one is a bad trade. Only pick this up once `evals` has a clean validation run (skills-7k7.7) behind it.

What stays in assurance and does not move into `evals`: the grader, rubrics, `checks.sh` scorecards, and `grade_report.py`. `evals` runs cells and captures output; it does not judge.

## Acceptance Criteria

`src/assurance/evals/run.sh` no longer carries its own copy of the cell, the assurance eval still produces an equivalent report, and there is exactly one implementation of the clean-room setup in the repo.
acceptance_criteria: run.sh no longer carries its own copy of the cell, the assurance eval still produces an equivalent report, and there is exactly one implementation of the clean-room setup in the repo.

title: make test is red on main — compile.py requires pd-components/package.json in synthetic repos
description:
`make test` is red on `main` and has been since commit `1c466e3` ("Decouple beta-planning skills from pd-components"). Two of the four assurance compiler tests fail.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
cd /home/vscode/src/skills
uv run pytest src/assurance/tests/ -q
```

Observed: `2 failed, 2 passed`, both failures `FileNotFoundError` on `pd-components/package.json` at `src/compile.py:124`.
Expected: 4 passed.

Reproduces from a clean checkout of `main` — no uncommitted changes are required.

## The failure

`TestIndexRegenerates::test_index_regenerates` and `TestRealModuleCompiles::test_real_module_compiles` both die at `src/compile.py:124`:

```
FileNotFoundError: .../test_real_module_compiles0/repo/pd-components/package.json
```

`_read_pd_version()` unconditionally reads `<repo>/pd-components/package.json`, but those tests build synthetic temp repos that do not contain a `pd-components/` directory.

## Confirmed pre-existing, not concurrent work

Established while running the evals epic (skills-7k7):

- `_read_pd_version` is **byte-identical** in `HEAD` and the working copy — the only uncommitted change to `src/compile.py` is at line ~733 (module registration for `new-task-quick`) and does not touch this code path.
- `src/assurance/tests/test_compiler.py` is unmodified.
- So both sides of the failure are committed code.

Compiling from the real repo root is unaffected — `uv run --no-dev python src/compile.py` succeeds and emits 36 skills. The breakage is confined to compiles rooted at a synthetic path, i.e. exactly what these tests do.

## Why it matters beyond the two tests

Several issues in the evals epic gate on "`make test` stays green". With `main` already red, that gate cannot distinguish a real regression from the standing failure — every agent has to be briefed on which failures to ignore, which is precisely how a genuine regression slips through unnoticed.

## Likely fix

Either make `_read_pd_version` tolerate a missing `pd-components/package.json` (returning `None` and having templating fail only if a skill actually references `{{ pd-version }}`), or have the test fixtures write a minimal `pd-components/package.json`. The first is probably right: a synthetic repo with no pd-components is a legitimate configuration, and the compiler should not require the file unless something needs it.

## Verification

`uv run pytest src/assurance/tests/ -q` → 4 passed. `uv run --no-dev python src/compile.py` from the repo root still emits 36 skills unchanged, and `git diff --stat skills/` after a compile shows no unintended churn.

## Acceptance Criteria

`make test` is green from a clean checkout of `main`, and compiling from the real repo root produces byte-identical output to before the fix.
acceptance_criteria: make test is green from a clean checkout of main (4 passed), and compiling from the real repo root produces byte-identical output to before the fix.
